audit.whatIsWrong: The diff enum reads 'FAV' while tone is the red #ff5d6c, diffRating is 8/10, breakdown.difficulty says 'Hard matchup' and report[14] says 'Hard matchup'.
audit.why: Four fields say hard and one enum says favoured. Three of the four are prose the user can read on the page, and the tone colour is already the hard-matchup red, so the enum is the outlier.
audit.corrected: diff 'FAV' -> 'HARD'. Enum field, exempt from the length band.

audit.whatIsWrong: win[4], win[5], win[6] and the matching phases[].side all read 'Skill' while whys[4] says 'Level 6 flips to you', whys[5] says 'you walk him down and kill on contact' and whys[6] says 'you're immune to his poke and delete him'.
audit.why: Those three why-lines are unambiguously Dr. Mundo-favoured, and late[] repeats it: 'Level 6 and 2+ items flip it hard to you.' The packet is explicitly flagged defective for this matchup ('level chart contradicts data: Dr. Mundo wins 52.14% but the chart gives Ziggs 5/7 stages vs 2'), so the packet chart is not the arbiter — but giving Dr. Mundo the three stages his own text already claims is what resolves that flagged contradiction with a 52.14% win rate.
audit.corrected: Three flips as one atomic group across both layers, ratings raised to 6/7/8. The why-lines already state the Dr. Mundo case and are left untouched.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hexplosive Minefield's diminishing-damage rule is absent, and Mega Inferno Bomb is called a 'long-range execute'.
audit.why: Riot's text on the minefield: 'Successive mine detonations on the same target deal reduced damage.' That is the whole answer to being zoned by it — a health-stacking tank should walk straight through in one line, because each additional mine hits him for less, and the worst thing he can do is back out and re-enter fresh. Nothing on the page said this; the mines were presented as a wall. Mega Inferno Bomb, meanwhile, has no execute component in Riot's text at all — it is 5000-range area damage where 'enemies in the primary blast zone take more damage than those farther away', so the outer ring is survivable. Calling it an execute tells a tank to fear the one thing he can eat.
audit.corrected: report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns now carry the diminishing mines; report[11].t turns it into the concrete instruction; spikes[1].text drops 'execute' and states the centre-vs-edge falloff with the 120s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Satchel Charge was listed as 24s in breakdown.cooldowns and report[5]. Hexplosive Minefield's cooldown was never given.
audit.why: Satchel Charge is 20/18/16/14/12 — four seconds shorter than stated at rank 1 and half the stated figure maxed. The minefield is a flat 16s at every rank, which makes it the more reliable zoning tool of the two and the one worth tracking.
audit.corrected: 20s at rank 1 / 12s maxed, plus the minefield at a flat 16s.

edits.before: - Ziggs Satchel Charge (24s): matchup-defining — His knockback + self-peel escape. Engage when it's down. Track it before every commit. - Your ultimate: spend it on kill windows, never on waves. - Summoners: track his Flash after any close call — it changes every dive call.
edits.after: - Ziggs Satchel Charge (20s at rank 1, 12s maxed): his knockback escape — engage when it is down. - Hexplosive Minefield (flat 16s): repeat mines on the same target deal reduced damage, so walk straight through it. - Your ultimate: kill windows only. - Track his Flash.

notes: Best new fact in this matchup: successive mine detonations on the same target deal reduced damage. For a health-stacking tank that inverts the correct play — walk through the minefield in one line rather than backing out and re-entering fresh — and it was nowhere on the page. Mega Inferno Bomb was also described as an execute, which Riot's text does not support; it is falloff area damage. Satchel Charge's cooldown was wrong at every rank.
unverified: The page repeatedly claims Ziggs deals percent-max-health damage (whys[3] 'percent-HP poke', spikes[0] 'percent-max-HP magic damage every wave'). The kit file carries a percentHealth flag on Satchel Charge, but Riot's own W description says only 'deals magic damage to enemies, knocking them away' with no health scaling, and nothing on Q or E suggests it either. Per the derived-flag rule I did not build new advice on that flag, and I did not delete the existing claims — they may be right. Worth one check before the next pass.

diff 'FAV' -> 'HARD' assumes the three prose fields (tone, diffRating 8/10, 'Hard matchup') are the intended reading rather than the enum. If the enum was the deliberate one, then diffRating, tone, breakdown.difficulty and report[14] all need to move the other way instead.
